claims.text: The draft describes lowering the delivery pod from the aircraft via a winch line.
claims.statement: The draft describes lowering the delivery pod from the aircraft via a winch line.
claims.quote:
The pod is released from 
the Zipline UA and lowered to the ground via the winch line.
claims.scope_note: Proposed workflow in a Zipline-prepared draft under FAA supervision; not proof of a particular observed delivery.

claims.text: During descent, the pod automatically controls its lateral position and evaluates the delivery location.
claims.statement: During descent, the pod automatically controls its lateral position and evaluates the delivery location.
claims.quote:
During pod descent, the pod 
automatically controls its position laterally and evaluates the delivery location.
claims.scope_note: The draft does not specify the AI model, computer vision method or camera architecture.

claims.text: If the delivery location is clear, the pod would continue descending and deliver the payload.
claims.statement: If the delivery location is clear, the pod would continue descending and deliver the payload.
claims.quote:
If the delivery 
location is clear, the pod would continue to descend and deliver the payload at the delivery 
target.
claims.scope_note: Conditional proposed workflow, not guaranteed delivery success.

claims.text: If the pod cannot automatically identify the target and evaluate its suitability, an image is sent to an operator for real-time evaluation.
claims.statement: If the pod cannot automatically identify the target and evaluate its suitability, an image is sent to an operator for real-time evaluation.
claims.quote:
If the pod is unable to 
automatically identify the delivery target and evaluate its suitability, an image is sent to an 
operator for real-time evaluation.
claims.scope_note: Operator escalation is conditional on failed automatic identification/evaluation; do not describe merely an unclear image or imply no oversight.

claims.text: If the delivery site fails Zipline’s evaluation criteria, delivery would stop and the pod would retract into the aircraft.
claims.statement: If the delivery site fails Zipline’s evaluation criteria, delivery would stop and the pod would retract into the aircraft.
claims.quote:
If the delivery site does not meet Zipline’s evaluation 
criteria,22 delivery would not continue, and the pod is retracted back into the Zipline UA.
claims.scope_note: The pod retracts; the document does not specify that the package then returns to its merchant or where the next attempt occurs.

claims.text: Zipline’s site criteria include visual obstacle clearance and may include checks for pod position tracking errors.
claims.statement: Zipline’s site criteria include visual obstacle clearance and may include checks for pod position tracking errors.
claims.quote:
Zipline’s evaluation criteria includes visual clearance for obstacles. It may also include additional checks such as 
pod position tracking errors.
claims.scope_note: Footnote 22; describes criteria without specifying the recognition algorithm.

claims.text: Zipline seeks approval to begin commercial package delivery operations in Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston, and San Antonio.
claims.statement: Zipline seeks approval to begin commercial package delivery operations in Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston, and San Antonio.
claims.quote: Zipline International Inc. (Zipline) is seeking FAA approval to begin commercial package delivery operations in five Texas metropolitan areas: Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston, and San Antonio.
claims.scope_note: Dallas is outside this named five-metro draft proposal.

claims.text: The FAA requests comments on the Zipline Texas draft environmental assessment by October 11, 2026.
claims.statement: The FAA requests comments on the Zipline Texas draft environmental assessment by October 11, 2026.
claims.quote: Please review the Draft EA and submit your comments by October 11, 2026.
claims.scope_note: Independently fetched current FAA page on edition date October 1, 2026; public comment window remains open.

claims.text: Zipline prepared the draft environmental assessment under FAA supervision.
claims.statement: Zipline prepared the draft environmental assessment under FAA supervision.
claims.quote:
Zipline prepared this draft environmental assessment (draft EA) under the supervision of the 
FAA7 to evaluate the potential environmental impacts that might result from the proposed
claims.scope_note: FAA-hosted primary document containing the applicant’s proposed operating description.

claims.text: The proposal cannot be implemented without FAA approval of the requested operating-specifications change.
claims.statement: The proposal cannot be implemented without FAA approval of the requested operating-specifications change.
claims.quote:
Without FAA approval of the requested OpSpecs 
modification, Zipline would be unable to implement this expansion of its delivery service.
claims.scope_note: Draft review does not constitute operating approval or proof that the five-metro expansion has occurred.

claims.text: Zipline’s current Droid perception recruiting description links multiple-camera inputs and 3D perception ML models to delivery and package pickup.
claims.statement: Zipline’s current Droid perception recruiting description links multiple-camera inputs and 3D perception ML models to delivery and package pickup.
claims.quote: You’ll build realtime 3D perception ML models that transform multiple camera inputs into scene geometry and semantics that help our mission planner with delivery and package pickup.
claims.scope_note: Employer job description for Droid autonomy that powers backyard delivery; updated September 28, 2026. It establishes corporate ML/perception specificity, not independent verification of the proposed Texas deployment architecture or that each draft site evaluation is performed by that exact model.

rejected.claim: This five-metro draft expands deliveries around Dallas
rejected.reason: The FAA names Amarillo, Austin, El Paso, Houston and San Antonio; Dallas is not included in this draft.

rejected.claim: The draft identifies AI cameras or computer vision as the delivery-site evaluation mechanism
rejected.reason: Full independently fetched 194-page PDF contains no artificial intelligence or computer vision description. It describes automatic evaluation and an image sent to an operator; camera/model specificity is not established by this draft.

rejected.claim: An unclear image automatically goes to an operator
rejected.reason: The exact condition is inability to automatically identify the target and evaluate its suitability; the draft does not specify an image-clarity trigger.

rejected.claim: The five-metro expansion is approved or successfully operating
rejected.reason: Current FAA page seeks approval and comments on a draft environmental assessment. Proposed operations are not demonstrated rollout results.

rejected.claim: Every attempted delivery succeeds without human oversight
rejected.reason: The draft explicitly provides operator escalation and retraction when evaluation criteria fail. No measured success rate has been verified.

rejected.claim: A failed delivery sends the package back to the merchant
rejected.reason: The evidence establishes retraction into the aircraft, not the subsequent destination of that payload.
